P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer of Gaunt Street, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and old friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. Enfield showed him a sinister door and told of a man who trampled a child. Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, who had never heard of Hyde. Utterson kept watch by the by-street door until he accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He then learned from Poole that Jekyll was out and that Hyde had a key. He now fears Jekyll is in deep waters.

P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. He has a key to Jekyll's house, comes by the dissecting room door, and all servants are ordered to obey him. He now mostly uses the laboratory and never dines there.

P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old school and college friend of Mr. Utterson and a friend of Dr. Jekyll. He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.
